what_it_does: The collection layer converts physical phenomena (reflected light, thermal emission, radar backscatter, RF emissions, sound, seismic vibration, AIS/ADS-B broadcasts, open web content) into data products (imagery, tracks, detections, emitter geolocations, signals metadata) that downstream processing, exploitation and dissemination (PED), fusion, and command-and-control layers consume. It spans sensors (EO/IR cameras, SAR, GMTI radar, passive RF receivers, microphone arrays, unattended ground sensors, sonobuoys), the platforms that carry them (satellites, Group 1-5 UAS, crewed aircraft, ships, USVs, towers, dismounted soldiers), the tasking/collection-management function that decides where sensors look, and the commercial data marketplaces that increasingly sell collection as a service. The economically decisive shift of 2022-2026 is that collection is now partly a bought commodity (NRO EOCL/RCA, NGA Luno, Space Force TacSRT, Army UAS marketplace) rather than only a government-owned capability.

current_architecture.description: A layered but stove-piped collection enterprise: national/commercial space (NRO-managed EOCL/RCA feeds flowing through NGA and Maven), theater airborne ISR (MQ-9, HADES/ATHENA, Triton) with service PED cells, brigade-and-below organic sUAS whose EO/IR video mostly terminates at the controller or a TAK client, and installation/base sensors (radar, passive RF, acoustic, towers) feeding C-UAS C2 (FAAD C2, Anduril Lattice, Dedrone, etc.). Commercial tasking reaches tactical users through TacSRT and the Global Data Marketplace, or through NGA channels; licensing tiers govern redistribution. TITAN is the Army's designated node to pull space, high-altitude, aerial and terrestrial sensor data into targeting.

current_architecture.security_domain: Commercial space and OSINT products are unclassified with license-tier restrictions (EOCL/Luno tiers govern redistribution to allies); tactical sUAS video is typically unclassified/CUI; TITAN, Maven and airborne multi-INT operate up to SECRET/SCI with cross-domain guards; passive RF and acoustic C-UAS sensors at installations operate unclassified but their detection libraries and performance data become CUI or classified.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Space and airborne collection depend on satellite downlink and enterprise networks; TITAN and brigade cells depend on SATCOM/tactical networks that are bandwidth-limited; sUAS depend on line-of-sight RF links that are jammed; commercial tasking marketplaces are cloud-hosted and reachable only with internet or enterprise connectivity.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Commercial tasking requests and product downloads stall (products are cloud-delivered); TITAN loses the space and high-altitude feeds it exists to fuse; sUAS video cannot be forwarded beyond the controller; C-UAS sensor nets fall back to local alerting without cross-cueing; analysts revert to manual, local exploitation (INFERENCE from architecture; no session-verified exercise quote).

technical_difficulty.summary: Building sensors and platforms is hard and capital-heavy (optics, SAR RF chains, radiation-tolerant electronics, launch, NOAA licensing, ITAR); the software adjacent to collection (tasking, cataloging, edge detection, sensor onboarding, ML classification of acoustic/RF signatures) is moderately hard and dominated by integration and data-access problems rather than algorithms. Passive RF and acoustic detection are signal-processing and ML problems on commodity hardware, but their credibility is proven only in government test events (T-REX, Falcon Peak, Eastern Shield), which cost time and relationships rather than money.
required_expertise: SAR processing and RF engineering (for SAR/RF sensing)
Array signal processing and beamforming (acoustic/passive RF)
Embedded ML on Jetson/FPGA at the edge
Geospatial data engineering (STAC, COG, NITF, KLV)
Cybersecurity for Blue UAS Framework listing
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Detecting and classifying small, RF-silent (fiber-optic or autonomous) UAS at useful range with near-zero false alarms from a dismounted or vehicle-portable passive sensor, and doing it cheaply enough to field at platoon scale; on the space side, the hardest unsolved problem is not collection but timely, license-compliant delivery of commercial products to tactical users without connectivity.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: MEMS microphones, SDR receivers (USRP, RTL/Lime class), Jetson-class edge compute, Teledyne FLIR Boson/Hadron thermal cores, COTS gimbals, LTE/mesh radios, cloud GEOINT stacks (STAC catalogs), open-source CV models; commercial imagery itself via vendor APIs at hundreds to thousands of dollars per tasking.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: Software-only (tasking aggregation, catalog/search, edge CV on existing sUAS video): $30k-$150k. Acoustic or passive-RF sensor node prototype on commodity hardware: $100k-$400k. Sensor payload for Group 1-2 UAS: $150k-$600k. Any satellite: $5M+ before launch and not feasible at $250k.
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: Software: $200k-$800k (Blue UAS Framework listing, ATO-adjacent hardening, participation in a JCO or Army test event, travel and GFE integration). Passive sensor hardware: $1M-$4M (ruggedized units, multi-site test at T-REX/Falcon Peak-type events, FCC/NTIA coordination if any emission). Satellite: $30M-$150M.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: Software: $1M-$5M (ATO, sustainment, on-site integration engineers). Sensor hardware at installation scale: $5M-$25M working capital (Hidden Level required roughly a decade and multiple test events before a $100M OTA). Constellation: $100M+.
capital_intensity.assumptions: Assumes two founders with $250k can reach POC only in the software or commodity-sensor lanes; assumes access to a sponsor for test events, which is unpriced but rate-limiting; assumes no classified facility. Hardware estimates are INFERENCE from comparable startups' disclosed raises (Hidden Level, Squarehead, Echodyne) and are LOW-MEDIUM confidence.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - commercial imagery (Planet, BlackSky, Umbra open data), open AIS/ADS-B, public drone acoustic datasets and self-collected sUAS video allow a full unclassified prototype; note that a credible C-UAS prototype needs live drone flights under FAA Part 107 and, for detection ranges, access to a test range.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for POC. Required for a credible demo: government test events (T-REX, Falcon Peak, JCO demos, Eastern Shield-type allied tests) and, for tasking products, access to TacSRT/GDM or NGA licensing terms. Classified signature libraries are required only for SIGINT-adjacent work (out of scope).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Remote sensing spacecraft fall under USML Category XV; many IR/thermal imaging systems above thresholds and fire-control-adjacent sensors under Category XII; military UAS and payloads under Category VIII; SIGINT/RF surveillance electronics under Category XI. Commercial-grade thermal cores (Boson class) and SDRs are typically EAR 6A/5A controlled rather than ITAR. Software that is purely commercial-imagery tasking/search is generally EAR99 or EAR-controlled at most. A specialist export-control review is required before any hardware or defense-article software work; this is a description, not a legal judgment.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes for anything touching installation sensor layouts, detection performance, Blue UAS cybersecurity artifacts, or unit collection plans; commercial-imagery tasking metadata is often CUI once tied to military users.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Likely for TITAN, Maven and airborne multi-INT integration (SECRET/SCI); avoidable if the product stays on the commercial-data and unclassified installation-security side, as Hidden Level and BlackSky's unclassified Luno services show.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for unclassified commercial-data or sensor MVPs; a cleared engineer or partner becomes necessary at first classified integration.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A German founder who becomes a US permanent resident is a US person for ITAR/EAR deemed-export purposes and SBIR ownership counting; an Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot receive ITAR technical data or certain EAR technology without a license, cannot hold a personnel clearance, and creates FOCI questions for any facility clearance. SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the concern to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (or eligible US entities), so the cap table matters. Mitigations to review with counsel: keep the product on commercial, unclassified data (EAR99-adjacent), assign the non-US founder to commercial/international roles, use a technology control plan, and consider allied-market (NATO, Indonesia is not a close partner for ITAR purposes) go-to-market. These are constraints requiring specialist legal review, not conclusions.

why_not_solved.explanation: Sensors and satellites need $30M-$1B; the three EOCL primes and three RCA holders already absorbed that capital and hold multi-year positions. New entrants compete for NRO study money, not operational buys.

Collection is bought by NRO, NGA, Space Force (TacSRT/JCO), Army PEOs, SOCOM and CBP under different vehicles and license regimes; TacSRT's zero FY2026 request shows no single budget owner for tactical commercial ISR.
The most valuable collection (SIGINT, GMTI, national imagery) is classified, so the unclassified startup wedge is confined to commercial data, C-UAS and OSINT lanes.
Vendor tasking APIs, Skydio's closed payload/cloud ecosystem, Palantir's TITAN/Maven stack, and Anduril's Lattice each own an integration seam and have little incentive to open it.
Blue UAS listing, ATOs, NOAA remote-sensing licenses and export controls slow every hardware entrant; the DIU-to-DCMA move is an admission the process did not scale.

Cheap edge ML, commodity SAR, and mass drone production (SkyFoundry) are 2023-2026 developments; RF-silent fiber-optic FPVs only became a mass threat in 2024-2025, creating the acoustic/passive-RF demand now reflected in the 2026 RFI.

For space-based EO/SAR/RF supply, the market is served and consolidating (Capella acquired, HawkEye IPO, Vantor rebrand). For installation-level passive RF, Hidden Level is scaling. Absence of startups in those lanes is not opportunity.

attractiveness.bull: Collection is now a bought commodity with real, recurring money (EOCL, RCA, Luno orders, $76.8M via GDM, $192M TITAN, $52M X10D, $100M Hidden Level OTA). The Army is flooding units with drones and sensors faster than it can ingest their data, DCMA is turning Blue UAS into a marketplace that needs vetted sensors and software, and the Army is openly asking for dismounted acoustic detection. Commodity hardware plus ML lets a small team prototype a passive sensor or a sensor-data product for well under $250k, and the government's own GAO says commercial data is underused because of access friction, which is a software and licensing problem.
attractiveness.bear: Every funded lane already has a scaled or scaling incumbent (Vantor/Planet/BlackSky, Capella/Umbra/ICEYE, HawkEye, Palantir, Anduril, Skydio, Hidden Level). Building sensors is capital-intensive and ITAR-adjacent, which is poor fit for a $250k team with a non-US-person founder. The tasking/aggregation gap is being filled by the government itself (TacSRT/GDM) and by the vendors' own platforms, and TacSRT's budget history shows tactical commercial ISR still lacks an owner. Dismounted acoustic detection is at RFI stage with no US program, and NATO-fielded Squarehead is ahead. Data access to sUAS video and TITAN is controlled by primes.
attractiveness.verdict: Low-to-medium for this team. Do not build sensors or satellites. The only defensible wedges are software that sits between commodity or commercial collection and the user: (a) acoustic/passive detection ML on commodity hardware aimed at the Army's 2026 dismounted RFI, accepting hardware exposure, or (b) sensor-agnostic ingestion/indexing of organic sUAS collection, which depends on OEM data access. Both are MEDIUM-confidence hypotheses that later stages should red-team.

signal_sequence.event: production - NRO EOCL awards to Planet, BlackSky, Maxar (5-year base + options to 2032)
prototype solicitation / study - NRO Commercial Radar Capabilities three-phase study begins (Jan 2022); Skydio selected for SRR PoR under 5-year OTA (Feb 2022)
prototype / pilot - Space Force TacSRT pilot marketplace begins; JCO begins Global Data Marketplace purchases
prototype award - Palantir TITAN prototype OTA ($178M, RECALL); NGA Luno A ($290M) and Luno B ($200M) IDIQ selections; Skydio X10D enters SRR Tranche 2

follow-on / repeat - Luno A delivery orders to BlackSky (up to $24M, $5M), Ursa ($21M); TacSRT expansion; NRO 15.5-month extensions to HawkEye 360, Capella, ICEYE, Umbra (Dec); FY2026 request omits TacSRT; HASC directs PoR; Blue UAS list to DCMA (Dec 3)
RFI - Army C5ISR acoustic detection RFI (Jan 14); SOCOM Tactical X RFI (Jan 30)

production / repeat - Skydio $52M+ order (Mar); BlackSky Luno A renewal (Mar); Army UAS marketplace adds Group 3 and payloads; Hidden Level $100M OTA (Jul 30); NRO RCA operational SAR contracts (Aug 1); TITAN $192M production orders (Sep 1); GAO-26-107959 (Aug 27)

market_stage.rationale: Across five years the sequence shows study/pilot vehicles converting into production or operational buys (EOCL, RCA, TITAN, SRR, Luno orders, Hidden Level OTA), which is the signature of a transitioning market; the exception is tactical commercial ISR access (TacSRT), which has demonstrated demand but no stable budget line, and acoustic/dismounted C-UAS, which is at RFI stage.

proto_purgatory.notes: TacSRT: pilot since 2023, praised as working, expanded in 2025, then zero-funded in the FY2026 request and rescued only by HASC language; that is a pilot-after-pilot pattern caused by budget ownership, not technology. Commercial SAR: four years of study contracts before operational awards, and 2 of 5 entrants dropped. VLEO/hyperspectral/thermal startups (Albedo, Pixxel, Hydrosat) remain on NRO SCE study contracts and SBIR/STRATFI awards without production (RECALL, LOW). Blue UAS: many listed vendors, but orders concentrate on Skydio. Counter-example: Hidden Level moved from test events to a $100M OTA within about a year of T-REX 25.2/Falcon Peak 25.2.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Mixed. For tactical commercial ISR access it is a warning (no budget owner; the government builds its own aggregator). For passive/acoustic C-UAS it is closer to opportunity (fresh RFI, recent conversion precedent). For new space sensors it is a warning for a small team.

candidate_gaps.title: Dismounted low-cost passive (acoustic + RF) detection of Group 1-2 and RF-silent UAS
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Small units have no cheap, non-emitting way to detect and classify small drones, including fiber-optic/autonomous RF-silent ones, and the Army opened an RFI for it in January 2026.
candidate_gaps.user: Dismounted squads/platoons, forward CPs, convoy escorts; secondary: installation security and allied forces
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Soldier hears or sees a drone. 2) RF detectors (DroneShield, Dedrone) alert only if the drone emits. 3) Radar is vehicle or site mounted and emits. 4) Alert is shouted or pushed to ATAK if a C2 link exists. 5) Engagement by small arms or handheld effector.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vehicle/site radars (SRC, Echodyne), RF detectors, installation passive RF (Hidden Level), NATO-fielded Squarehead Discovair, improvised Ukrainian phone-based acoustic nets
candidate_gaps.failure_point: RF detection fails on RF-silent drones; radars emit and are not dismount-portable; acoustic systems are either large arrays or unfielded in US service; false alarms and range are unproven at platoon scale

evidence.claim: Army C5ISR Center RFI seeks acoustic detection of Group 1 and 2 UAS for dismounted troops to inform requirements and prototyping
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD awarded a $100M OTA to Hidden Level after T-REX 25.2 and Falcon Peak 25.2 for passive sensing that detects RF-silent aircraft, showing budget and procurement path for passive detection at installation scale
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Poland tested seven acoustic detection systems under Eastern Shield; Norway contracted Discovair; UNIFY.C2 integrated Squarehead in Sep 2026: multiple companies attempting partial solutions, none scaled in the US
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Ukraine fielded thousands of cheap acoustic sensors (Sky Fortress-type) to detect Shahed-class and small UAS, demonstrating a low-cost architecture
evidence.label: INFERENCE (RECALL - not re-verified this session)

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Detection performance must be proven at government test events that take a year or more to enter; acoustic classification needs large labeled datasets of drone signatures in realistic noise; incumbents bundle detection into C2 suites; the US requirement only crystallized in 2026.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: Hidden Level can add microphones; DroneShield/Dedrone can add acoustic modules; Squarehead can enter US via a partner (already with UNIFY.C2).
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: ML classification on a commodity MEMS microphone array plus SDR on a Jetson-class board, sold as a cheap networked node with CoT/ATAK output, competing on cost per node and software rather than array hardware; data flywheel from many deployed nodes.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Four-to-eight mic array plus SDR in a ruggedized box under $1,500 BOM; on-device classifier trained on self-collected and public drone acoustic datasets; publishes detections as CoT to ATAK; demo against Part 107 flights of representative Group 1 drones, then seek C5ISR Center or JCO test slot.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Labeled acoustic and RF signatures across drone types, distances and noise environments; self-collectable for commercial drones, but military-relevant signatures require test-event access
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: CoT/ATAK, FAAD C2 or Lattice/other C-UAS C2 interfaces; Blue UAS Framework-style cyber vetting for software; MOSA/SOSA optional
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: C5ISR Center RFI follow-on prototyping, JCO demonstrations, Army xTech, SBIR (subject to ownership eligibility), allied tests (Eastern Shield-type)
candidate_gaps.why_now: RF-silent fiber-optic drones since 2024-2025; Army Drone Dominance and C-UAS reorganization; 2026 RFI; DCMA marketplace lowers listing friction
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Hardware-intensive with a non-US-person founder (ITAR Category XI/XII exposure if it becomes a defense article) and range/false-alarm physics that a small team may not beat; incumbents add acoustic as a feature.
